I've taken a look at your requirements for a CS student laptop, and based on what's available, I found a great option that seems like a fantastic fit for you: the Lenovo IdeaPad 3 (11th Gen Intel Core i3).

Power & Performance: It sports an 11th Gen Intel Core i3 processor (with 2 cores and 4 threads, boosting up to 4.1 GHz) paired with 8GB DDR4 RAM (which is awesome because you can actually upgrade it to 12GB if you ever feel the need!). Plus, you get a speedy 512GB SSD, meaning quick boot-ups and applications loading in a flash – super handy when you're juggling VS Code, browsers, and class materials.
For Your Classes & Coding: The 15.6" Full HD display is great for coding without squinting, and the HD 720p camera with a privacy shutter and dual mic is perfect for those online classes. No more worries about your background!
Portability & Battery: It's quite thin (1.99 cm) and light (1.7 kg), so tossing it in your backpack won't be a pain. And with up to 7 hours of battery life and Rapid Charge, you won't always be hunting for a power outlet.
Software Ready: It comes pre-loaded with Windows 11 Home and Office Home and Student 2021, so you're good to go right out of the box. You even get a 3-month Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscription, which is a nice bonus!
A Quick Note for Docker & Heavier Tasks: The i3 processor and 8GB RAM are definitely capable for coding, VS Code, and light Docker containers. For a CS student just starting out or working on smaller projects, it should serve you well. However, as you progress and potentially work on more complex projects with multiple, resource-intensive Docker containers, you might eventually find yourself wishing for a processor with more cores or even more RAM. But for your current needs and budget, it's a very solid starting point!

What do other users think? People who own it describe it as "quite fast and snappy" and "good for students, home use activities." They love the fast boot time and good audio quality for classes. Just a heads-up, some users mention all the ports are on one side and it doesn't have a Type-C port, which is something to consider if those are important to your workflow.

All in all, given the options available, the Lenovo IdeaPad 3 really stands out as the best fit for your budget and requirements as a CS student. It's a capable machine that will get you started strong!
